newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Senate head sees cabinet reshuffle useful.
newsitem.headline: French Senate head sees cabinet reshuffle useful.

text.p: French Senate President Rene Monory called on Thursday for a cabinet reshuffle that would leave Prime Minister Alain Juppe in place but bring in committed pro-Europeans.

"I believe that we need the biggest pro-Europe majority possible in government," Monory, a member of the centrist UDF party which is the junior partner in France's ruling coalition, told LCI television.
"If there was to be a reshuffle, it should come relatively quickly. I'm not talking of a reshuffle which would see the departure of Juppe," he said.
Monory added that the new government should be smaller, and that Juppe should give new recruits more autonomy than their predecessors.

Asked if he was in favour of supporters of former Prime Minister Edouard Balladur entering the government, such as ex-ministers Nicolas Sarkozy and Francois Leotard, Monory answered: "Why not? But if it's people who want to break up Europe, then I don't agree."

Earlier, Monory told Europe-1 radio that he was not aware of any imminent reshuffle of the centre-right government. He said shuffling ministers might be a useful move to break France out of a mood of pessimism.

Juppe, whose popularity has tumbled because of record unemployment of 12.6 percent and budget austerity to help France qualify for a single European currency from 1999, has faced widening criticism of his rule.
Monory said he believed changing prime ministers would not be useful because whoever headed the government would be unpopular due to France's austerity policies.
"I have always said that whoever was prime minister would be unpopular," he said.

On Wednesday, a source at President Jacques Chirac's office said rumours of an imminent change had no foundation. "If there is a reshuffle, it would probably be at the start of 1997," the source said.
